sources.label: WICG manifest-incubations PR #136: Add spec language for PWA Origin Migration
Chrome sample: Web App Origin Migration

syntax.rationale: The old-origin manifest JSON block contains the page's migration_target declaration grammar; the field name and URL shape disagree with the merged incubation specification as recorded in notes.

inputs.rationale: The manifest-fields table identifies the old manifest as the input and describes the destination manifest URL value.

outputs.rationale: The migration sequence describes the resulting prompt and, on acceptance, an updated installed-app identity with preservation where possible.

errors.rationale: The constraint-check block explicitly labels a cross-site move BLOCKED; the page also describes enterprise-blocked migration in the workflow.

context.rationale: The section requires cooperation from the old and new origins and describes Chrome's installed-PWA migration workflow.

lifecycle.rationale: The step table sequences declaration, confirmation, user prompt and acceptance or decline; these are the page's described lifecycle.

examples.rationale: The page has a pre/code JSON old-origin manifest example; its non-same-site destination and field name differ from the cited specification (see notes).

compatibility.rationale: The browser-support table names Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; the Chrome release/status divergence is retained in notes.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The section ties old/new-origin confirmation to hijack prevention and describes the enterprise policy block; see notes for the additional association-file requirement in the specification.

syntax.rationale: The new-origin manifest JSON block contains the page's migration_source declaration grammar; the field name and value shape disagree with the merged incubation specification as recorded in notes.

inputs.rationale: The manifest-fields table identifies the new manifest as the input and describes its reference back to the old manifest.

outputs.rationale: The step table describes the paired declaration triggering the user-facing migration prompt and the accepted identity update.

errors.rationale: The constraint-check block explicitly marks cross-site migration BLOCKED; the workflow separately describes enterprise suppression of the prompt.

context.rationale: The workflow requires cooperation between the old and new origins; neither can redirect an installed PWA alone according to the page.

lifecycle.rationale: The workflow sequences new-origin confirmation after old-origin declaration and before Chrome's offer and the user's decision.

examples.rationale: The page has a pre/code JSON new-origin manifest example; its non-same-site origin and field name differ from the cited specification (see notes).

compatibility.rationale: The browser-support table states Chrome 147 trial, Edge tracking Chromium, and no Firefox or Safari signal; see notes for source disagreement.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The section calls the new-origin confirmation a hijack prevention step and describes enterprise policy suppression; see notes for spec validation details absent from the page.

notes: Fetched 2026-10-06: the page calls the old/new manifest members migration_target and migration_source with string manifest URLs, while merged WICG manifest-incubations PR #136 defines migrate_to as an optional object with id and install_url and migrate_from as a list of IDs or objects (with id, install_url and optional behavior); neither side is adjudicated here. Fetched 2026-10-06: the page's two JSON examples use app.example.com and app.newexample.com and label the pair same-site, while merged WICG PR #136 requires both manifest ID origins to be same-site and illustrates old.example.com to new.example.com; neither side is adjudicated here. Fetched 2026-10-06: the page says the reciprocal manifest declarations suffice to prevent hijacking, while merged WICG PR #136 also requires the old origin to host /.well-known/web-app-origin-association authorizing the new manifest ID with allow_migration true; neither side is adjudicated here. Fetched 2026-10-06: the page calls Chrome 147 a developer trial behind chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, while ChromeStatus feature 5123349239955456 states Chrome 150 introduces migration, lists desktop implementation milestone 147 and desktop launch milestone 150, and the linked Chrome sample labels Chrome 147+ and directs testers to chrome://flags/#web-app-migration-api; neither side is adjudicated here. Fetched 2026-10-06: the page asserts Edge 147 is tracking Chromium, while ChromeStatus feature 5123349239955456 lists Chrome, Firefox and Safari positions but no Edge status; neither side is adjudicated here. IN-UNIT PROSE REPAIR (coord 22:30Z): every divergence above is now disclosed ON THE PAGE, both sides with their values and the fetch date inside each sentence, and the specification divergence is pinned in the curated table in scripts/source-disagreement.test.mjs. VERIFIED BY THE IMPLEMENTER before the page carried any of it: PR #136's own diff defines migrate_to/migrate_from (16 and 18 occurrences) and contains migration_target/migration_source ZERO times, plus 12 references to web-app-origin-association and 2 to allow_migration; ChromeStatus 5123349239955456 shows developer-trial stage desktop 147 and ACTIVE ship stage desktop 150 with status Proposed, accurate_as_of 2026-07-21. The examples' member names and value shapes are a page-content defect beyond a disclosure, filed separately rather than silently rewritten under a contract unit.
